text:
TECHNOVA Information Security and Data Protection Policy 2026 

Effective Date: January 15, 2026 
Version: 1.0 
Approved By: Executive Leadership Team and Chief Information Security Officer (CISO). 

1.0 Introduction and Objectives 
1.1 Introduction 
In a modern technology environment, securing corporate digital assets and client data is 
fundamental to business operations. At Technova, we prioritize data privacy, network resilience, and 
robust risk management. 
1.2 Purpose and Scope 
This document outlines the official Information Security and Data Protection Policy for Technova. The 
primary objective is to define a comprehensive framework that protects Technova's information 
assets from all internal, external, deliberate, or accidental threats. This policy applies to all full-time 
and part-time employees, contractors, interns, vendors, and third-party partners who access 
Technova’s corporate networks, computing hardware, cloud infrastructures, or physical premises. 
1.3 Our Core Security Philosophy 
We view information security not as a restrictive barrier, but as an enabling foundation for 
engineering excellence and customer trust. Our security philosophy centers on three core pillars: 
• 
Confidentiality: Ensuring that sensitive systems and private data are accessed only by 
authorized personnel with a legitimate business need. 
• 
Integrity: Protecting information from unauthorized modifications, accidental tampering, or 
malicious corruption to maintain complete data accuracy. 
• 
Availability: Guaranteeing that authorized users have reliable, uninterrupted access to the 
technology infrastructure and engineering applications they need to execute their daily 
work. 
1.4 Compliance and Regulatory Alignment 
Technova aligns its security practices with leading international technology frameworks and data 
privacy standards. This structure ensures that our internal operations comply with relevant local and 
international regulations governing data governance, consumer privacy, and digital infrastructure 
protection. 
2.0 Access Control and Identity Management 
2.1 Access Control Guidelines 
Controlling who can interact with Technova's internal systems reduces our attack surface and 
prevents unauthorized data exposure. 
2.2 The Principle of Least Privilege

id: CH_TECHNOVA  Information Security and Data Protection Policy 2026_A13CD0_C0
text:
Technova enforces the Principle of Least Privilege across all software environments, code 
repositories, and administrative tools. This means that access rights are strictly limited to the bare 
minimum resources required for a team member to complete their specific job duties. Role 
modifications resulting from internal promotions, team transfers, or departmental changes must be 
updated immediately in our corporate directory. 
2.3 Identity Verification and Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) 
All network access to Technova corporate accounts requires strong identity verification. 
• 
MFA Requirement: Multi-Factor Authentication is mandatory for all employees and 
contractors accessing any corporate system, including email, HRIS portals, code 
environments, and cloud consoles. 
• 
Password Standards: Passwords must meet or exceed our modern complexity guidelines, 
requiring a combination of uppercase letters, lowercase letters, numbers, and special 
characters. Passwords must never be reused across separate accounts. 
• 
Shared Accounts: The use of generic or shared group logins is strictly prohibited. Every 
action taken on Technova networks must be traceable to an individual authenticated 
account. 
2.4 Privileged Access Reviews 
Access permissions for high-level administrative accounts, root environments, and core databases 
are subject to continuous monitoring. Human Resources and IT Infrastructure teams conduct formal 
access alignment reviews every quarter to ensure old permissions are stripped away when roles 
change. 
3.0 Device Security and Workstations 
3.1 Endpoint and Workstation Protection 
Every laptop, workstation, and mobile device connected to Technova’s internal networks serves as a 
critical point of protection. 
3.2 Corporate Hardware Allocation 
Employees must perform all work-related duties, software development, and client communications 
exclusively on company-issued computing hardware. Personal devices (laptops, tablets, desktop 
computers) are strictly prohibited from connecting to Technova’s private production environments or 
core development networks. 
3.3 Endpoint Management Protocols 
All company-provided hardware is pre-configured with standardized corporate endpoint security 
software managed directly by our Central IT team. 
• 
Security Software: Endpoint detection, automated firewalls, and corporate anti-malware 
utilities must remain actively running at all times. Employees are strictly prohibited from 
disabling or modifying these applications. 
• 
Software Patching: Operating systems and professional software utilities must be updated 
promptly when corporate alerts are pushed. Critical patches must be installed within 48 
hours of notification.

text:
• 
Encryption: Full-disk encryption is mandatory and automatically enabled on all company-
issued laptops to safeguard data in the event of physical theft or loss. 
3.4 Clear Desk and Lock-Screen Discipline 
When leaving your workstation or desk for any duration—even briefly—you must lock your operating 
system screen via keyboard shortcuts or system menus. Physical documents containing confidential 
code, client information, or project strategies must never be left exposed on desks and must be 
stored securely in locked filing cabinets when not in use. 
4.0 Data Classification and Privacy 
4.1 Data Classification Framework 
To protect information efficiently, Technova categorizes data into clear classification levels based on 
its sensitivity and the potential risk of exposure. 
4.2 Tier 1: Public Data 
This category covers information that is intentionally approved for open public consumption. 
Examples include public marketing copy, open career opportunities on our company job board, and 
standardized technical documentation. Exposure of this data presents zero risk to Technova or its 
clients. 
4.3 Tier 2: Internal Operations Data 
This category involves day-to-day business operational data intended exclusively for internal team 
members. Examples include standard operating procedures, non-proprietary engineering templates, 
and internal announcements. Unauthorized external exposure could cause minor operational 
inconvenience but no structural harm. 
4.4 Tier 3: Confidential Corporate Data 
This tier handles sensitive business data that must be kept confidential to protect Technova's 
marketplace position. Examples include corporate financial ledgers, product development roadmaps, 
proprietary source code, and employee personnel files. Unauthorized exposure could lead to severe 
financial or reputational damage. 
4.5 Tier 4: Restricted Client Data 
This represents our highest sensitivity tier, encompassing all client-owned data, production database 
records, consumer personal identifiable information (PII), and authentication keys. This data must 
remain isolated in encrypted storage environments and can only be accessed during active, 
authorized client engineering workflows. 
5.0 Network Security and Data Transmission 
5.1 Network and Communication Safeguards 
Protecting how data travels across internal systems, local offices, and remote spaces prevents 
interception and unauthorized network access. 
5.2 Remote Connection Standards 
Working from remote locations requires secure communication channels to keep corporate traffic 
isolated from public utility hazards.

id: CH_TECHNOVA  Information Security and Data Protection Policy 2026_D4B1DA_C0
text:
• 
Corporate VPN: Employees working remotely must utilize the official corporate Virtual 
Private Network (VPN) with multi-factor authentication active before accessing any internal 
asset. 
• 
Public Wireless Networks: Connecting to open, public, or unencrypted Wi-Fi networks (such 
as those found in cafes, hotels, or airports) while handling Technova business is strictly 
prohibited unless routed completely through the corporate VPN. 
5.3 Encryption in Transit and at Rest 
All Tier 3 (Confidential Corporate) and Tier 4 (Restricted Client) data must be heavily encrypted 
wherever it moves or is stored. Communication protocols used by our applications must enforce 
modern secure transport layers to safeguard text, API keys, and code updates. 
5.4 Technical Case Study: Insecure Wi-Fi Hazards 
• 
Scenario: An engineer working on a software update at a local coffee shop connects their 
company laptop directly to the shop’s unencrypted public Wi-Fi network without turning on 
their corporate VPN. 
• 
Analysis: This action violates our security protocol. Operating on an open public network 
without a VPN exposes the machine to local interception attacks, potentially allowing 
malicious actors on the same network to monitor clear-text system traffic or harvest active 
session cookies. 
• 
Correct Action: The engineer must activate their secure corporate VPN before connecting to 
any network outside Technova’s private facilities, ensuring all outbound and inbound packets 
are completely encrypted. 
6.0 Software Development and Cloud Security 
6.1 Secure Engineering and Infrastructure 
As a technology company, building security directly into our development lifecycle prevents software 
vulnerabilities and cloud misconfigurations. 
6.2 Secure Coding Standards 
Our engineering teams must adhere to standardized secure coding practices throughout product 
development cycles. This includes validating all input parameters to prevent injection bugs, sanitizing 
output variables, utilizing approved cryptographic libraries, and ensuring authentication methods 
cannot be bypassed. 
6.3 Code Repository Governance 
All proprietary code bases must be hosted within Technova’s authorized secure repositories. 
• 
Secret Management: Hardcoding system passwords, API tokens, database connection 
strings, or SSH keys inside application source code repositories is strictly prohibited. All 
credentials must be managed via dedicated, secure environment secret managers. 
• 
Peer Reviews: All software code updates must undergo a mandatory peer-review process 
and pass automated security vulnerability scans before being merged into active production 
branches.

6.4 Infrastructure and Cloud Isolation 
Technova's production environments are completely isolated from our daily testing and development 
sandboxes. Actual client production data must never be copied, cloned, or downloaded down into 
development or testing environments under any circumstances. 
7.0 Incident Response and Threat Management 
7.1 Threat Identification and Reporting 
Early detection of unusual system behavior, phishing attempts, or physical breaches minimizes 
potential impact and speeds up resolution. 
7.2 Defining a Security Incident 
A security incident is any observable event that compromises our core pillars—such as unauthorized 
access to corporate accounts, active malware infections, laptop theft, suspicious data transfers, or 
potential exposures of client files. 
7.3 Immediate Reporting Procedure 
If you observe a security threat, notice strange behavior on your machine, or accidentally click a 
suspicious link in a phishing email, you must act immediately. 
• 
Report to Security: Send a detailed update directly to our security response team via the 
designated internal dashboard or alert email. 
• 
Include Details: Provide the names of affected systems, exact error messages, screenshots if 
possible, and a brief description of the event. 
• 
Avoid Self-Remediation: Do not attempt to run third-party cleaning tools or manually delete 
system logs yourself, as this can destroy critical evidence needed for forensic investigation. 
7.4 Incident Response Case Study: Phishing Link 
• 
Scenario: An operations specialist receives an email that looks like an urgent request from a 
core vendor asking them to reset their account password. They click the link and enter their 
corporate Technova credentials before realizing the sender domain is fake. 
• 
Analysis: This constitutes an active security compromise that threatens corporate credentials 
and network access. 
• 
Correct Action: The specialist must immediately report the compromise to the security team 
and change their password via our central system right away. The security team will instantly 
terminate all active sessions on that account to block unauthorized entry. 
8.0 Physical and Workplace Security 
8.1 Physical Facility Safeguards 
Digital security depends heavily on physical access controls. Protecting our offices and server rooms 
prevents physical tampering and unauthorized equipment modifications. 
8.2 Badge Discipline and Access Gates 
Access to all Technova office buildings and secure engineering areas is controlled by electronic badge 
access gates.

id: CH_TECHNOVA  Information Security and Data Protection Policy 2026_8DC5BB_C0
text:
• 
Individual Badges: Employees must wear their corporate identity badges visibly at all times 
while on company premises. Badges must never be shared or loaned out to anyone. 
• 
No Tailgating: Tailgating—the practice of following another person through a secure door 
without scanning your own badge—is strictly prohibited. Every individual must scan their 
own badge at every entry point. 
8.3 Visitor Management Framework 
All non-Technova personnel, including clients, vendors, delivery staff, and job applicants, must be 
registered as visitors at the front reception desk. Visitors must be issued a temporary visitor badge 
and must remain accompanied by a full-time Technova employee at all times while moving through 
our corporate facilities. 
8.4 Secure Areas and Server Facilities 
Areas holding core local network routers, physical server components, or storage backups are 
designated as high-security zones. Access to these spaces is strictly limited to authorized network 
administrators and requires multi-level authorization logs. 
9.0 Vendor Management and Third-Party Risk 
9.1 Third-Party Risk Governance 
Our security posture is deeply connected to the software applications, SaaS tools, and external 
vendors we utilize to conduct daily operations. 
9.2 Security Due Diligence 
Before Technova integrates any external software tool, cloud platform, or vendor utility into our 
technical operations, the vendor must undergo a formal review by our security evaluation team. 
Vendors must provide verifiable proof of modern security practices, data privacy compliance, and 
robust data encryption standards. 
9.3 Contractual Protections 
All external corporate agreements must include strict data protection clauses. Vendors handling any 
Tier 3 or Tier 4 data are contractually required to report any security or data breach impacting 
Technova systems within 24 hours of discovery. 
10.0 Governance, Administration, and FAQs 
10.1 Individual Employee Obligations 
• 
Complete all mandatory security awareness training modules promptly. 
• 
Identify, flag, and report suspicious emails, system behaviors, or badge violations 
immediately. 
• 
Keep your company-issued laptop physically secure and log out when stepping away. 
10.2 Technical Management Obligations 
• 
Ensure that engineering updates follow our peer review and code validation rules. 
• 
Verify that your team members possess only the access rights required for their active 
project tasks.

10.3 Policy Enforcement and Penalties 
Adherence to this security policy is mandatory for everyone working with Technova. Failure to 
comply with these safety guidelines can expose the company to regulatory fines or data exposure, 
and may lead to disciplinary action up to termination of employment. 
10.4 Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 
Q1: Can I use my personal computer for engineering work if my company laptop is updating? 
A: No. Connecting personal, unmanaged hardware to Technova's core code repositories or 
development sandboxes is strictly prohibited to prevent data leakage and system vulnerabilities. 
Q2: What should I do if I suspect a colleague is using an unapproved cloud application to store 
code? 
A: Storing corporate assets or project source code in unvetted external cloud applications bypasses 
corporate access controls. You should flag this issue directly to your manager or report it to our 
security review team. 
Q3: Is it acceptable to write my network passwords on a sticky note if I keep it inside my desk 
drawer? 
A: No. Writing down passwords or authentication keys on physical media creates a physical security 
vulnerability. All credentials should be recorded exclusively in our approved corporate password 
manager utilities.
